title: Painting Estimating Software: 8 Tools for Faster, Cleaner Bids
html:
Painting estimating software turns a walkthrough into a priced proposal, and the right one depends on how you price. Pick PaintScout for production rates, Joist or Wave for simple bids, or Contractor Foreman for plan takeoffs. Published plans here run from $0 to $199 a month.

A painting bid is a small math problem with a lot of ways to go wrong. Square footage, coats, prep hours, trim and materials all change the number. Estimating software fixes the math, but it cannot fix a bad rate.

This guide sorts eight tools by how they build the estimate. Every price comes from the vendor page linked beside it, read in November 2026, and each tool gets one real limit.

Which painting estimating software prices by production rate and takeoff?

PaintScout and Contractor Foreman are the two tools here that build estimates from measured quantities. One is made for painters, and one is built for general contractors who also paint.

  • PaintScout: production rate estimating with material lists, pre-built templates, photo uploads, optional upgrades, change orders and interactive proposals with eSignature. The Sales plan is $119 a month billed monthly or $99 billed annually. Limit: the page does not state how many users each plan includes, so confirm seats first.
  • Contractor Foreman: estimates with bulk and line-item markups, plan upload with measured takeoffs, and online client approval. Standard is $139 a month billed monthly or $105 billed annually, for up to 3 users. Plus is $199 monthly for up to 8 users. Limit: the page does not say which plans include takeoffs, and Basic and Standard have no local material pricing.
ToolHow it builds an estimateEntry price shownUsers
PaintScout SalesProduction rates and material lists$119 monthly, $99 billed annuallyNot stated
Contractor Foreman StandardLine items, markups and plan takeoff$139 monthly, $105 billed annuallyUp to 3
Contractor Foreman PlusSame, with more seats$199 monthly, $166 billed annuallyUp to 8

Published list prices from each vendor page, November 2026. Taxes, add-ons and card fees are extra.

A production rate is how much area one painter covers in an hour. Painting software multiplies area by that rate to get labor hours. If your default rate is faster than your crew, every bid is too low.

Check how each tool handles waste and coverage. Paint coverage per gallon varies by surface and product, so a tool that lets you edit coverage per line beats one with a fixed number.

Takeoff matters most on commercial work. Measuring hallways and offices from a plan beats walking each room twice. For a typical house repaint, a room-by-room form in a tool like PaintScout is faster than uploading plans.

Cost lines matter as much as labor. Paint, primer, tape, plastic and caulk add up on a large job, and a template that leaves them out hides the gap until the invoice. Add a supplies line as a percent of materials, using your own receipts.

Contractor Foreman lists an AI estimator that drafts an estimate from project details, marked as a preview. Treat any draft as a starting point and check the rates before you send it.

Which estimate apps suit a small painting crew on a budget?

Joist, Wave and Workiz handle simple estimates for a small crew. None of them knows painting rates, so you supply the numbers. That is fine if you already price from your own spreadsheet.

  • Joist: estimates that convert to invoices, online payments and homeowner financing. Pro is $17 a month billed monthly with unlimited documents. Elite is $32 monthly and adds change orders. Limit: Basics allows only 5 documents a month, and the free plan is no longer offered.
  • Wave: Starter is $0 and Pro is $19 a month billed monthly, and both allow unlimited estimates and invoices. Card payments on Starter cost 2.9% plus 60 cents. Limit: it has no painting rates, takeoffs or crew scheduling.
  • Workiz: scheduling, jobs and estimates on Standard, Pro and Ultimate, with unlimited clients and estimates on every plan. Limit: the page shows request pricing instead of a price, so the cost is unknown until you ask.

Change orders are the painter's quiet profit leak. A homeowner adds a ceiling or a second coat on site, and the work happens without paper. Joist lists change orders on Elite, and PaintScout lists them in its estimating features.

Joist also lists homeowner financing, and PaintScout lists Wisetack financing. Offering a monthly payment on a large exterior can move a hesitant buyer. Check the lender terms yourself, because the software vendors do not set them.

If you only send a handful of bids a month, the free Wave plan is hard to beat on price. If you bid every week, the time saved by templates and eSignature pays for a paid tool.

Can field service apps send painting estimates?

Yes. Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz all send estimates, and Jobber and Housecall Pro tie them to scheduling and payments. They suit painters who want quotes, crews and invoices in one app.

  • Jobber: quotes, invoices and online payments. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. Grow adds richer quotes with images and optional upsell line items and starts at $199 a month for one user billed monthly with no commitment. Limit: extra users are $29 a month each.
  • Housecall Pro: estimates and invoicing on every plan. Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user. The sales proposal tool is listed on Max at $299 a month billed annually. Limit: add-on prices are not published.

Quote structure matters here. Good, better and best options let a homeowner pick a level without asking for a discount. A single flat number invites a negotiation, and a three-option bid invites a choice.

Upsell line items fit painting well. A quote that offers trim, a ceiling or a garage door as optional extras lets the homeowner say yes to more. Jobber lists optional line items on Grow, and PaintScout lists optional upgrades.

Photos help the estimate too. Jobber lists images on richer quotes on Grow, and PaintScout lists photo uploads. A picture of peeling trim in the proposal explains the prep line better than a paragraph.

Which tools automate follow-ups after you send a painting estimate?

Jobber Connect and HubSpot Starter automate follow-ups, so a sent estimate does not sit unanswered. Most lost painting bids are not rejected, they are forgotten.

  • Jobber Connect: automated quote and invoice follow-ups, automated client reminders and QuickBooks Online sync. Connect for one user is $139 a month with no commitment, or $99 billed annually. Limit: follow-ups start on Connect, so Core users send them by hand.
  • HubSpot CRM: the free plan covers up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts. Starter adds automation and is listed at $20 per seat a month, with new-customer pricing of $7 billed annually or $10 billed monthly. Limit: free email sends are capped at 2,000 a month.

A simple cadence works: a thank-you the day of the walkthrough, a nudge three days after the proposal and a last check a week later. Keep each message to two sentences and offer one clear next step.

Track the response rate by bid size. Small interior bids may close on a text, while exteriors often need a second visit. Once you see which bids stall, you can set a different cadence for each one.

Keep the first message personal. Mention one detail from the walkthrough, such as the color the homeowner picked or the rotted trim you flagged. A generic template reads like every other bid in the inbox.

Automation should never replace a phone call on a large job. Use it for the first two touches, then call. A voice on a $9,000 exterior bid closes more than a third email.

How should you build a painting estimate template?

Build one template per job type, with your own rates in it. Interior walls, ceilings, trim, doors, cabinets and exterior siding each need their own line and their own production rate.

  • Measure: wall area, ceiling area, linear feet of trim and count of doors and windows.
  • Prep: a separate labor line for patching, sanding, caulking and masking, since prep is where bids go wrong.
  • Coats: primer and finish coats priced separately, with a note on the paint line and sheen.
  • Materials: gallons from coverage on the can label, plus supplies and a waste allowance.
  • Markup and terms: overhead, profit, deposit and what counts as a change order.

Here is an example only, not a benchmark. Say your crew covers 150 square feet of wall an hour. A 600 square foot room is then 4 hours of painting labor before prep. Replace both numbers with your own tracked rates.

Write your exclusions into the template. State that furniture moving, drywall repair beyond minor patching and lead paint work are separate. Clear exclusions protect your margin and reduce arguments after the first coat.

Track real hours on every job for a month. Compare the estimate to the actual time and adjust each rate. After a few jobs your template is better than any default in any software.

What does painting estimating software cost each month?

A solo painter can estimate for $17 a month, and a commercial bidder lands near $199. These totals use plan fees only, so card fees and taxes come on top.

SetupPartsMonthly plan cost
Solo painter, simple bidsJoist Pro billed monthly, Wave Starter for the books$17
Residential repaint crewPaintScout Sales billed monthly$119
Crew with follow-up automationJobber Connect for one user, billed monthly with no commitment$139
Commercial bidder with takeoffsContractor Foreman Plus billed monthly, up to 8 users$199

Built from the vendor prices above, November 2026. Annual billing lowers each figure but ties you to a year.

Compare the monthly cost to one lost bid. Suppose a better estimate wins one extra interior job a quarter. Then even the $199 plan can cost less than the work it wins. That is a decision rule, not a promise.

How do you choose painting estimating software?

Choose painting estimating software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it price by area and production rate, handle change orders, and send a proposal your client can sign on a phone?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then compare the total against one average interior bid.

Setup effort: can you enter your rates and a template in a weekend, or does it need onboarding?

A solo painter pricing by the room should start with Joist Pro or Wave. A residential crew that bids by square foot fits PaintScout. A company that bids offices and new builds from plans should test Contractor Foreman.

Estimates only help if bids arrive. Ads from painter Google Ads and rankings from painter SEO bring requests in, and a clear painter website turns visitors into walkthroughs.

What is the best estimating software for painters?

There is no single best tool, because it depends on how you price. PaintScout is built for painting production rates. Contractor Foreman adds plan takeoffs. Joist and Wave suit simple bids. Run each free trial on two real bids before you decide.

How much does painting estimating software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $199 a month for Contractor Foreman Plus billed monthly. Joist Pro is $17 a month billed monthly, and PaintScout Sales is $119 monthly. Card fees and extra seats cost more.

Is there free painting estimating software?

Wave Starter is $0 and allows unlimited estimates and invoices. It has no painting rates or takeoffs, so you bring your own numbers. The HubSpot free CRM covers lead tracking only and sends no estimates. Joist no longer lists a free plan on its published plans.

Can painting estimating software handle change orders?

Some can. PaintScout lists change orders in its estimating features, and Joist lists them on Elite at $32 a month billed monthly. Confirm that a change order can be signed on a phone, since most changes happen on site, not at your desk.

What should a new painting contractor use first?

Start with Wave Starter at $0 or Joist Pro at $17 a month, plus your own rate sheet. Move to PaintScout when you bid every week and want production rates and proposals. Do not pay for takeoffs until you bid from plans.

Build one template per job type, with your own rates in it. Interior walls, ceilings, trim, doors, cabinets and exterior siding each need their own line and their own production rate.
-
Measure:
wall area, ceiling area, linear feet of trim and count of doors and windows.
-
Prep:
a separate labor line for patching, sanding, caulking and masking, since prep is where bids go wrong.
-
Coats:
primer and finish coats priced separately, with a note on the paint line and sheen.
-
Materials:
gallons from coverage on the can label, plus supplies and a waste allowance.
-
Markup and terms:
overhead, profit, deposit and what counts as a change order.
Here is an example only, not a benchmark. Say your crew covers 150 square feet of wall an hour. A 600 square foot room is then 4 hours of painting labor before prep. Replace both numbers with your own tracked rates.
Write your exclusions into the template. State that furniture moving, drywall repair beyond minor patching and lead paint work are separate. Clear exclusions protect your margin and reduce arguments after the first coat.
Track real hours on every job for a month. Compare the estimate to the actual time and adjust each rate. After a few jobs your template is better than any default in any software.

How do you choose painting estimating software?
Choose painting estimating software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
does it price by area and production rate, handle change orders, and send a proposal your client can sign on a phone?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then compare the total against one average interior bid.
Setup effort:
can you enter your rates and a template in a weekend, or does it need onboarding?
A solo painter pricing by the room should start with Joist Pro or Wave. A residential crew that bids by square foot fits PaintScout. A company that bids offices and new builds from plans should test Contractor Foreman.
Estimates only help if bids arrive. Ads from painter Google Ads and rankings from painter SEO bring requests in, and a clear painter website turns visitors into walkthroughs.
###
What is the best estimating software for painters?
There is no single best tool, because it depends on how you price. PaintScout is built for painting production rates. Contractor Foreman adds plan takeoffs. Joist and Wave suit simple bids. Run each free trial on two real bids before you decide.
###
How much does painting estimating software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $199 a month for Contractor Foreman Plus billed monthly. Joist Pro is $17 a month billed monthly, and PaintScout Sales is $119 monthly. Card fees and extra seats cost more.
###
Is there free painting estimating software?
Wave Starter is $0 and allows unlimited estimates and invoices. It has no painting rates or takeoffs, so you bring your own numbers. The HubSpot free CRM covers lead tracking only and sends no estimates. Joist no longer lists a free plan on its published plans.
###
Can painting estimating software handle change orders?
Some can. PaintScout lists change orders in its estimating features, and Joist lists them on Elite at $32 a month billed monthly. Confirm that a change order can be signed on a phone, since most changes happen on site, not at your desk.
###
What should a new painting contractor use first?
Start with Wave Starter at $0 or Joist Pro at $17 a month, plus your own rate sheet. Move to PaintScout when you bid every week and want production rates and proposals. Do not pay for takeoffs until you bid from plans.
